mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate level signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated unemployment rates above 4.0% indicate a weakening labor market and economic slowdown, which typically triggers negative equity returns as corporate earnings face downward pressure over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of 20-day periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous low federal funds rates and high inflation (CPIAUCSL) signal stagflationary risks, causing equity markets to discount higher future interest rates and economic uncertainty, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect fails when the joint condition (FEDFUNDS < 2.0% and CPIAUCSL > 255.0) produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST above 1300.0) reflect strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which typically support positive equity returns as corporate revenues and profits rise over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of 20-day periods when HOUST exceeds 1300.0, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Robust consumer spending (RSAFS above 500,000 million dollars) indicates strong household demand and economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS exceeds 500,000, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production below 100.0 indicates a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain activity, which typically leads to negative equity returns as corporate output and profits decline over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of 5-day periods when INDPRO falls below 100.0, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent low employment growth (PAYEMS below 150,000) and rising unemployment (UNRATE above 3.5%) signal a deteriorating labor market, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings pressure.
failure_condition: The joint signal fails when PAYEMS < 150,000 and UNRATE > 3.5% produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL above 255.0) indicates a persistent inflationary environment that typically triggers aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise and economic growth slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of 20-day periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 255.0, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.
